content.text:
Yes, I redrew the [Article page](https://claude.ai/artifact/VwamEgzZtjde1M1GW1gWWC#artboard-Article) using the Memorisely article's layout, in your cream, Recoleta and teal rather than their dark look.

**What I took from it:**
- **Breadcrumb bar:** "Articles / I write articles now?" sits between thin lines under the nav.
- **Header:** a small teal "Writing" pill (the label your articles page already uses), then a bigger 60px title, the description as a lede, and an author row: an "SN" initials circle, your name, and the date and read time. The Listen button sits at the end of that row, and a thin line closes the header.
- **Two columns:** the article text stays a readable width (680px max) on the left, with a 340px sidebar on the right. On a phone the sidebar drops below the article.
- **Sidebar cards**, teal-bordered like your homepage cards:
  - **More articles:** a "View all" link and rows with a title, date and chevron.
  - **Working on something interesting?:** a line about what you do and an email button.
  - **RSS:** a "Follow along with RSS" link under the cards.

**What changed from the last version:**
- The bottom "More articles" section is gone, since the sidebar does that job now.
- The page container widens from 800px to 1120px to fit the two columns.

**What I assumed:**
- I used initials instead of a photo, since there's no avatar in the repo.
- On the real site I'd make the sidebar stick while you scroll, like theirs. The canvas can't show that.

**What I left alone:** I didn't copy their dark theme, their font, or their promo cards.

I write articles now?

Guessing I'm writing articles now, for the fun of the game.

S Sara November 22, 2026 · 2 minute read
Listen · read by Sara 0:42 / 2:10
1x

I used to write notes, scripts, life highlights inside a notebook this one specifically. It's the best time to embarrass myself on the internet, because why not?

It's not about writing things for people to read (at the end of the day it's going to be read by web scrapers duh) it's mostly about writing things that matter to the world. At least I hope. I hope this gives you a sense of life, reading something a human wrote for fun.

What I do

This is probably where it's more difficult to get into, because it's so complex that I don't even know what I do. Generally I'm a software engineer, full stack dev, IT whatever you want to call me with intent in focusing on.. everything.

I really like solving problems, but I also really really like telling people what to do and how to do it in the most efficient way possible.

questions.question: Your pages are already server-rendered HTML, built once at deploy time (static prerendering) and served by the Cloudflare worker. How should SSR work after the redesign?

options.label: Keep prerendering (Recommended)
options.description: Pages stay HTML rendered ahead of time, with no client-side rendering. This is the fastest to load, the easiest path to Lighthouse 100, and needs no new dependencies.

options.label: Per-request SSR, homepage only
options.description: Add the @astrojs/cloudflare adapter and render the homepage on each request, so the GitHub pinned repos are always fresh. Every other page stays prerendered. This adds a dependency and a slightly slower first byte on the homepage.

options.label: Per-request SSR everywhere
options.description: Render every page on the Cloudflare worker for each request. This is the biggest change: the adapter replaces parts of worker.ts and the markdown-twin build step has to be reworked. It also makes Lighthouse 100 harder.

#!/bin/sh
# Runs Lighthouse (mobile + desktop) on each page of the preview server, then summarizes.
# usage: run.sh <base-url> <out-dir>
BASE=$1
OUT=$2
mkdir -p "$OUT"
for page in "home:/" "articles:/articles" "article:/articles/i-write-articles-now" "services:/services" "privacy:/privacy"; do
  name=${page%%:*}
  path=${page#*:}
  for mode in mobile desktop; do
    preset=""
    [ "$mode" = desktop ] && preset="--preset=desktop"
    pnpm dlx lighthouse@12 "$BASE$path" $preset --quiet --output=json --output-path="$OUT/$name-$mode.json" \
      --chrome-flags="--headless=new --no-first-run" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "FAILED $name $mode"
  done
done
node "$(dirname "$0")/summary.mjs" "$OUT"

# PR Description

Draft a PR description from the current branch. Draft only: never push, never create the PR, never touch `master`/`main`.

## Steps

1. Find the base branch with shell, no Python:
   ```bash
   base=$(git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|origin/||')
   base=${base:-main}
   ```
2. Read what changed:
   ```bash
   git log "$base"..HEAD --oneline
   git diff "$base"...HEAD --stat
   git diff "$base"...HEAD
   ```
3. Check for dependency changes (`package.json`, lockfiles, etc.) and name any added or removed package.
4. Write the description using the format below. If the user supplied context (ticket, deadline, reviewers), use it verbatim.

## Format

The full template is in `references/template.md`. Fill only the sections that have real content. Terse is correct: a two-section description is fine when that is all there is to say.

- Status line: `READY FOR REVIEW` or `NOT READY`. Default to `NOT READY` unless the user says otherwise.
- Never invent Needed By, Urgency, JIRA tickets, or @mentions. Omit them, or leave a clearly marked `TODO` if the user asked for the full template.
- Steps to Test: derive from the diff only when the steps are obvious. Otherwise omit.
- Plain `-` markdown bullets. No emojis.
- Flag, but do not fix, unrelated issues noticed in the diff.
- One feature = one branch = one PR. If the diff spans unrelated features, say so instead of merging them into one summary.

## Example

```markdown
# TLDR
Functional Tests for All Documented Auth endpoints

# Additional information
added the @adonisjs/auth module
```

Match this tone: a one-line TLDR, then short factual notes (new dependencies, notable changes). No filler, no hedging.

## Output

Return the description in a single markdown code block so it can be copied as is.
